_comment: The captain's own life: events that ask who the captain is (captain_trait.X) and what they've given their life to (focus == X, data/focus.json). Choices that a trait cares about are tagged in the dialog and wear the trait down or build it up (scripts/nature.gd); "voice" here marks a stance the outcomes don't show. See docs/events.md.

cap_drunk_morning.title: The morning after
cap_drunk_morning.text: You wake on the cabin floor with the sun in your eyes. The mate says you came on deck in the middle watch, gave orders nobody could understand, and fell asleep against the binnacle.

choices.result: Some of them laugh with you. Not many.

choices.text: Swear off the bottle, in front of all of them
choices.result: It's the longest month of your life. But it holds.
choices.fail_result: It lasts four days. Everyone knows it lasted four days.

choices.result: The second bottle is better than the first.

cap_gambler_table.title: The back room
cap_gambler_table.text: There's a game in the back room of the best tavern in {port}: planters, a colonel, and stakes you could lose a ship on. You can hear the dice from the street.

choices.text: Sit down and play for {stake} a throw
choices.result: The colonel signs you a note for what he can't pay. You'll never see it. You don't care.
choices.fail_result: You lose, and double, and lose again.

choices.result: You walk away. Your hands shake all the way back to the boat.
choices.fail_result: You get as far as the door.

cap_devout_feast.title: A feast day
cap_devout_feast.text: It's a saint's day in {port} and the bells have rung since dawn. A devout captain doesn't work on a feast day, and your crew know you're one.

choices.text: Keep the feast: mass ashore, and no work
choices.result: The whole crew stands at the back of the church, scrubbed and awkward.

choices.text: Work through it. God understands cargo
choices.result: The bells go on ringing while you load. It sounds like an accusation.

cap_superstitious_bird.title: The white bird
cap_superstitious_bird.text: A white bird has followed the {ship} for three days, always off the starboard quarter. You don't like it. You don't like it at all.

choices.result: The crew go very quiet. You feel better. They don't.

choices.text: Heave to for a day, and let it go its way
choices.result: On the second morning it's gone. Everyone breathes.
It's a bird. It's only a bird. You say so, and they believe you.
choices.fail_result: You keep looking at it. So do they.

cap_hot_head_insult.title: Words at the next table
cap_hot_head_insult.text: A merchant captain at the next table in {port} says something about your ship, and your mother, and laughs.

choices.result: He doesn't laugh again. Neither does anyone else in the room.
choices.fail_result: He's a better brawler than he looked.

choices.result: You finish your drink and leave. It's harder than any fight.
choices.fail_result: You didn't mean to throw the table.

cap_coward_sail.title: A sail at dawn
cap_coward_sail.text: A strange sail at dawn, hull down and coming on. Probably nothing. Your hands are sweating, and the crew are watching your hands.

choices.result: She was a fishing smack. Everyone saw her through the glass by noon.

choices.text: Hold your course and let her come
choices.result: She was a fishing smack. You held your course anyway, and they saw that too.
choices.fail_result: Your voice cracks on the order. Nobody mentions it, all day.

cap_greedy_ledger.title: Counting twice
cap_greedy_ledger.text: The quartermaster has seen you counting the plunder twice, and the second count always comes out smaller.

choices.text: Take a captain's share and a half
choices.result: Nobody says anything to your face.

choices.text: Square the books, fair to the penny
choices.result: It hurts. The crew notice it hurts, and like you better for it.

cap_merciful_gallows.title: A hanging in the square
cap_merciful_gallows.text: They're hanging a boy in the square at {port}: {boy}, a cabin hand off a pirate sloop, fourteen at most. The crowd is in a holiday mood.

choices.text: Pay the hangman to cut the rope early (100 gold)
choices.result: The rope parts, somehow, and in the confusion {boy} ends up in your boat.
You talk about youth and mercy and the price of rope. The magistrate releases {boy} into your custody, to be rid of you.
You hear the drop from the quay.

cap_butcher_name.title: The Butcher
cap_butcher_name.text: The crew have started calling you the Butcher. Not where you can hear it, but you hear it.

choices.result: By the next port they're saying it where you can hear it, and they're saying it with pride.
You let the next prisoner go with a coat and a purse. Nobody knows what to make of it.

cap_old_messmate.title: An old messmate
cap_old_messmate.text: A {nation_adj} lieutenant stops dead in the street in {port}. You served together years ago, on the same gundeck, before you took to this.

choices.text: Buy them a drink and talk about old times
choices.result: Over the third bottle you learn where the squadron will be all month. Neither of you says why you're asking.

choices.text: Ask them to forget your face
choices.result: "What face?"
choices.fail_result: Duty is duty. Your description is in the admiral's letters by the week's end.

choices.text: Pretend you've never seen them before
choices.result: They let you. That hurts more than you expected.

cap_family_letter.title: A letter from home
cap_family_letter.text: A letter from home has caught up with you in {port}. Everyone is well, the roof leaks, and the money you sent last time is gone.

choices.result: You write a long letter with it. You're cheerful for a week.
It's what you can.
You read it twice more and put it away.

cap_seasick_storm.title: At the lee rail
cap_seasick_storm.text: The storm has you on your knees at the lee rail, in front of the whole watch.

choices.text: Stay on deck, white as a sail
choices.result: Sick or not, you never leave the deck. They respect that more than a strong stomach.
choices.fail_result: You last an hour, and then you don't.

choices.text: Go below and leave it to the boatswain
choices.result: The boatswain brings her through. The crew will remember who did.

cap_honest_oath.title: A small lie
cap_honest_oath.text: A merchant in {port} asks you to swear to the customs house that his cargo came over in your hold from Jamaica. It didn't. He'll pay well.

choices.result: The words come out easily. That's what bothers you.
He calls you a fool. He's probably right.

cap_schemer_letter.title: The wrong letter
cap_schemer_letter.text: A letter is delivered to your boat in {port} by mistake, sealed with the governor's arms.

choices.text: Lift the seal with a hot knife
choices.result: You reseal it so well that even you can't tell.
It goes on its way. You wonder about it for days.

focus_blade_master.title: A fencing master
focus_blade_master.text: A fencing master in {port} has watched you fight, and found a dozen things wrong. He offers lessons. Hard ones.

choices.result: A week of bruises. Then, one morning, you touch him first.

choices.text: Spar with him on the quay, for the crew to see
choices.result: The crew cheer every touch. So, in the end, does he.
choices.fail_result: He wasn't lying about the dozen things.

choices.result: He shrugs. His loss.

focus_blade_challenge.title: A challenge on the main deck
focus_blade_challenge.text: The biggest hand aboard says, in front of the whole watch, that a captain who fights in front ought to be able to put him down.

choices.text: Fists, now, on the main deck
choices.result: It doesn't take long. You help him up afterwards.
choices.fail_result: It takes a long time, and you're the one who gets helped up.

choices.result: He finds he has work to do somewhere else.

choices.text: Laugh, and give him an extra tot
choices.result: Everyone laughs. Nobody's sure who won.

focus_purse_ledger.title: Forty years of prices
focus_purse_ledger.text: A merchant in {port} who has lost everything offers to sell you his book: forty years of who pays what, where, and who can be leaned on.

choices.result: You read it every night for a month.
He sells it cheap, and almost thanks you. The book would have approved.
He'll find another buyer. Probably.

focus_purse_venture.title: A share in a venture
focus_purse_venture.text: A syndicate of merchants in {port} is sending a cargo of logwood to Amsterdam, and wants a partner with a fast ship and a good head for figures.

choices.result: The logwood sells high. Your share comes back doubled, with a letter asking you to join the next one.
choices.fail_result: The ship is lost off the Azores. So is your money. You learn something about syndicates.

choices.result: There will be other ventures.

focus_command_drill.title: Slow aloft
focus_command_drill.text: The new hands are slow aloft and slower on the braces. In a fight it will cost lives.

choices.text: Drill them, watch on watch, until they're fast
choices.result: They curse you for a week. Then they're the fastest topmen you've had.

choices.text: Go aloft yourself and show them
choices.result: The captain at the masthead, in a stiff breeze, laughing. They'll follow you up anything now.
choices.fail_result: The footrope is wet. The deck is hard.

choices.result: They will. Or they won't.

focus_command_table.title: The captain's table
focus_command_table.text: Your officers have stopped eating together. They pass each other on deck without a word.

choices.text: Dine them all in your cabin, and keep the wine coming
choices.result: By the end of the night they're arguing about a battle twenty years ago, all on the same side.
They don't.

focus_whisper_maid.title: The governor's maid
focus_whisper_maid.text: A maid at the governor's house in {port} is sweet on one of your sailors, and very talkative.

choices.text: Buy her ribbons, and listen (20 gold)
choices.result: Ribbons are cheap. What she tells you isn't.
She tells you about the governor's accounts, and the second set of accounts.
Your sailor is disappointed.

focus_whisper_tavern.title: Clerks in their cups
focus_whisper_tavern.text: Two clerks from the harbour office are drinking in a corner of a tavern in {port}, and talking too loudly about the navy's sailing orders.

choices.text: Stand them drinks, and keep them talking
choices.result: By midnight you know where every patrol will be for a month.
choices.fail_result: They clam up when they see who's buying.

choices.result: Loose talk. Someone else will hear it.
